answer: A seat cannot vote until a stranger knocks. At enrolment the operator registers a street address and locks 250 POA. A courier from a panel of forty arrives unannounced, scans a government ID and signs a receipt stamped with GPS and arrival time, paid $6.50 a stop. Seats sharing an address, an ID hash or a courier route fold into one vote; a refused visit forfeits the bond. A thousand hollow seats need a thousand doors and a thousand IDs, near $6,500 in fees an epoch. On a reef coral grips bare quartz where one larva lands, and the falcon on the cliff knows each ledge by its own scratches.
